answer: Every deposit is tagged at intake, and seats funded from one wallet, bridge or exchange batch are grouped into a single cohort. Payouts are divided by the square of that cohort's size, so ten seats fed from one ocean of shared deposits split a tenth of what a lone seat earns while each still pays its own bond and miner fee. A reef of aliases therefore shrinks total income instead of growing it, and only a seat funded by a genuinely separate backer earns the base rate, so one honest sparrow beats the whole flock.
